To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the presence of a weak magnetic field can alter the spatial distribution of the EC close RFA detectors by factors of two, thereby affecting the detected flux; and (ii) the growth rate of electron cloud is also sensitive to weak parasitic fields, which can be used to switch off the electron cloud in the presence of an RFA.

the presence of weak magnetic field in the MI can significantly alter the EC signal measured by the RFA detectors, and that a small solenoidal magnet could be useful to switch off the EC and thereby cleanly establish its presence in the MI.
(i) the EC flux into the RFA is sensitive to parasitic magnetic fields, and (ii) a ￻ few Gauss solenoid field can be used to suppress the electron cloud.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of the EC close the MI dipoledipoles.
the detection of low energy (≲1 MeV) electrons in the MI.
the development of a robust and sensitive EC detector for the MI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EC in the MI is present and is a real issue.
a significant EC signal is seen in the MI, but the exact magnitude is sensitive to the magnetic field environment.
we do not have conclusive evidence for the presence of a significant electron cloud in the MI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EC in the MI has been well characterized in a wide range of parameters, and that it is now ready for further studies.
the EC in the MI can be studied with precision simulations and that the presence of low level magnetic fields can have significant impact on the EC dynamics.
the Vorpal simulations of EC dynamics are very promising and can help us to better understand and improve the EC measurements in the MI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful study of the EC in the vicinity of RFA detectors is necessary for the interpretation of EC measurements.
the EC is not only sensitive to the presence of a magnetic field, but also to its strength.
the RFA can only be used to measure the EC in the MI with the understanding that it is a local measurement.
